raw_text:
- This study aims to investigate the reasons behind persistent completion-time differences across sites implementing similar nominal work processes. The focus is on identifying measurable factors that contribute to these differences and distinguishing between potential explanations.

Assumptions
- Sites with similar nominal work processes exhibit observable completion-time differences.
- Measurable factors influence the completion times.
- Observations can be used to discern between competing explanations.

Research design
- Quasi-experimental design using pre- and post-intervention measurements from multiple sites.
- Controlled for common inputs to isolate the effects of potential explanatory factors.

Data or evidence needed
- Completion times for identical tasks at different sites.
- Operational definitions of the nominal work processes.
- Baseline measurements before implementing changes.
- Observational data on identified factors affecting completion times.

Measurement
- Completion time: The time taken to complete a standardized task.
- Nominal work process: Defined and measured based on specific operational criteria.
- Factors: Personnel ratios, work environment conditions, task complexity, etc.

Analysis
- Descriptive statistics to summarize completion times and factor levels.
- Inferential statistics to assess differences in completion times across factor levels.
- Regression analysis to identify significant predictors of completion time.

Decision / stopping rule
- Statistical significance at the 0.05 level in regression analysis.
- Repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) to evaluate changes over time.

Limitations
- Variation in task variability across sites.
- Limited control over external factors influencing completion times.
- potential selection bias in site selection.
